notes: All six candidates confirmed via Crossref; none rejected, no duplicates.

Almog & Korngreen 2016: Europe PMC fullTextXML and NCBI efetch returned no body text (publisher-restricted); abstract from Crossref plus a partial read of the PMC HTML page (Challenge I only). Challenges II and III unverified.

Cafaro et al.: bioRxiv API lists v1 (2025-08-05) titled 'Degeneracy and bifurcation diversity at the single neuron level' and v2 (2025-11-01) with the candidate title; Crossref carries the v2 title. The title change between versions is reconcilable, not a conflict. bioRxiv pubs API found no published version.

Naudin 2023: no abstract in Crossref, PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, HAL API or Semantic Scholar (publisher elided). HAL PDF fetch returned an Anubis 'Access Denied' page; Springer page redirected to an auth endpoint. Content beyond title, keywords, PubMed publication type (Journal Article; Review) and a machine-generated Semantic Scholar TLDR is unverified.
GitHub unauthenticated REST API rate-limited mid-batch; the two Allen Institute repositories were confirmed with the authenticated gh CLI instead.

rows.citation: Trensch G, Gutzen R, Blundell I, et al. (2018). Rigorous Neural Network Simulations: A Model Substantiation Methodology for Increasing the Correctness of Simulation Results in the Absence of Experimental Validation Data. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics 12:81.
rows.model_type: Spiking neural network model (Izhikevich 2006 polychronization network) compared between its C implementation and a SpiNNaker neuromorphic reproduction
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares two independent implementations; time step and numeric data type are analysed as error sources, not generated as seeded single-fault mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - network driven by one saved random input series; five selected network states are compared, not a battery of stimulation protocols.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - statistical spike-train and population-dynamics measures via NetworkUnit/Elephant; no single-cell current-clamp features such as rheobase or sag.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - comparison measures and network states are chosen by the modellers; no selection or minimisation of tests.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - one worked example (one network, one reproduction); no held-out models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - human-made port to neuromorphic hardware; no AI-assisted transformation assessed.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Supplies verification/substantiation terminology and a statistical-equivalence workflow for one network re-implementation. NeuroSem would target edited single-cell NeuroML models with seeded mutants, current-clamp protocol fingerprints, refinement-calibrated tolerances and greedy battery selection tested on held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.3389/fninf.2018.00081 (title, 5 authors, vol 12, article 81, issued 2018-11-26); Europe PMC search (PMID 30534066, PMC6275234, OA) abstract and fullTextXML keyword-context read; GitHub REST API repos/INM-6/networkunit.
rows.found_via: Europe PMC 'test-driven AND (neuroscience OR neuron model)'; 'equivalence AND neuron model AND ... simulator'

rows.citation: Almog M, Korngreen A (2016). Is realistic neuronal modeling realistic? Journal of Neurophysiology 116:2180-2209.
rows.model_type: Multicompartment conductance-based layer 5 pyramidal neuron models (three published models; per PMC page read: Mainen & Sejnowski 1996, Schaefer et al. 2003, Hay et al. 2011)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - published models are challenged as released; no seeded faults or systematic single-change mutants in the abstract or accessible text.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - three computational challenges beyond original use; Challenge I is proximal apical dendritic current injection with axonal sodium block; others not read.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - qualitative comparison of somatic and dendritic spiking (e.g. isolated dendritic calcium spikes) with recordings; no standardised feature extraction.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - challenges are hand-chosen by the authors to probe model limits.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - challenges probe behaviour outside each model's original design targets, conceptually out-of-sample, but there is no formal held-out design.
rows.ai_transformations: no - review and critique of human-built models; no AI transformations.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Motivating critique: models that meet their original targets can fail new challenges. NeuroSem asks a different question, whether an edited model still matches its own reference, using automated protocols, features, mutants and protocol selection.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1152/jn.00360.2016 (title, 2 authors, vol 116, pp 2180-2209, abstract); Europe PMC search (PMID 27535372, PMC5102320, not OA; fullTextXML and NCBI efetch returned no body); WebFetch pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5102320 (partial, Challenge I only).
rows.found_via: Europe PMC '"simulator" AND "NeuroML" AND convergence AND comparison'

rows.citation: Gouwens NW, Berg J, Feng D, et al. (2018). Systematic generation of biophysically detailed models for diverse cortical neuron types. Nature Communications 9:710.
rows.model_type: Biophysically detailed conductance-based models with reconstructed morphologies and active somatic conductances for 170 mouse V1 neurons (Allen Cell Types Database)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - conductance densities are fitted by genetic algorithm; no deliberate fault seeding or mutant-detection analysis.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - trained on features of a single-amplitude step; evaluated on noisy current injection, slow ramps and series of depolarising steps.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - feature errors as absolute z-scores against experimental variability; spike-time explained variance for noise stimuli.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - stimuli are fixed by the experimental pipeline; optimisation is over model parameters, not protocol choice.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - generalisation tested on stimuli not used in fitting, classifiers cross-validated; no held-out models for detecting changes.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted editing or transformation of models.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Uses fit-on-one-stimulus, test-on-others logic for model-to-data agreement and releases models. NeuroSem would compare model versions against their own reference, with seeded mutants, refinement-based tolerances and battery selection; these models are candidate fixtures only after format and licence checks.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1038/s41467-017-02718-3 (title, 8 authors, vol 9, article 710, issued 2018-02-19, abstract); Europe PMC (PMID 29459718, PMC5818534, OA) fullTextXML read of model-generalisation, classification and code/data availability; gh api repos for AllenInstitute/biophys_optimize and AllenInstitute/AllenSDK.

rows.citation: Joshi N, van Der Burg S, Celikel T, et al. (2025). Neuronal identity is not static: An input-driven perspective. PLOS Computational Biology 21:e1013821.
rows.model_type: Experimental whole-cell recordings from mouse barrel cortex L2/3 neurons; GLIF models fitted only to extract passive attributes (not model regression)
rows.controlled_mutations: no - analyses recorded neurons; no model edits, faults or mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - compares step-and-hold with frozen-noise input generated from a simulated Poisson network, applied to real neurons rather than models under test.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - action-potential, waveform, GLIF-derived passive, adaptation-current and spike-triggered-average attributes extracted and used for clustering.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - two fixed input paradigms are compared; attribute sets are ranked by explained variance, but protocols are not selected.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - unsupervised classification analysis; no held-out model or fault-family design.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Empirical evidence that conclusions about neuronal behaviour depend on the input protocol. NeuroSem would apply that insight to regression testing of edited models, adding mutants, calibrated tolerances and optimised protocol batteries.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1013821 (title, 4 authors, vol 21, e1013821, issued 2025-12-22, abstract); Europe PMC (PMID 41428743, PMC12755851, OA) fullTextXML read of methods and data/code availability; GitHub REST API repos/Nishant-codex/single_cell_analysis.
rows.found_via: Europe PMC '"current clamp" AND "protocol" AND "neuron model" AND (informative OR optimal OR selection)'

rows.citation: Cafaro G, Bernard C, Hashemi M, et al. (2025). Degeneracy in neuronal bifurcation landscapes: equivalent bifurcation sequences across distinct parameter sets. bioRxiv (preprint, v2).
rows.model_type: Minimal conductance-based single-neuron model with three variable conductances (gNa, gCl, gK) under varied extracellular potassium
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - systematic sweeps of conductance parameter space group sets by bifurcation sequence; not single-fault mutants of a reference model.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - the varied condition is extracellular potassium; a figure compares parameter sets under a 100 pA current pulse and under elevated potassium.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - burst onset/offset features from simulated membrane-potential traces drive automated bifurcation-type classification; not standard current-clamp feature sets.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - no selection of stimuli or conditions for discriminating parameter sets.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - classifier built from manually labelled features; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Parameter sets alike under one condition can differ in transition thresholds under another, supporting the silent-drift premise and caution about equivalent mutants. NeuroSem would operationalise this for edited NeuroML models with stimulus batteries, tolerances and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref api.crossref.org/works/10.1101/2025.08.04.668451 (posted-content, v2 title, 4 authors); bioRxiv API details (v1 2025-08-05 with different title, v2 2025-11-01, CC-BY) and pubs endpoint (no published version); v2 JATS XML full-text keyword read; GitHub REST API repos/GianmarCafaro/Pattern_Detection.
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:biorxiv.org (conductance-based model degeneracy parameter sensitivity electrophysiological features)

rows.citation: Naudin L (2023). Different parameter solutions of a conductance-based model that behave identically are not necessarily degenerate. Journal of Computational Neuroscience 51(2):201-206.
rows.model_type: Conductance-based neuron models (short theoretical piece indexed as Review; specific model unverified)
rows.controlled_mutations: unclear - no abstract or full text accessible; keywords mention ion channel variability and parameter solutions, not mutant generation.
rows.protocol_optimization: unclear - full text not retrieved; nothing in title, keywords or record suggests protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - full text not retrieved; six-page Review is unlikely to include an evaluation design, but this is unconfirmed.
rows.ai_transformations: unclear - full text not retrieved; retrieved metadata gives no indication of AI-assisted transformations.
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Retrieved metadata and a machine-generated Semantic Scholar summary suggest it argues identical behaviour is insufficient for degeneracy, proposing shared bifurcation structure as a condition. Relevant caution for equivalent-mutant definitions; not a testing method.
